chunks.text: Kestrel Shipmanagement - Leave and Holiday Policy (HR-POL-01 v3.3)

chunks.heading: Version: 3.3
chunks.text:
Effective Date: 1 April 2026
Applicability: Shore-based Office Staff, Mumbai and Chennai Offices
Purpose and Scope
This policy establishes the framework for leave entitlements and holiday management for
shore-based staff at Kestrel Shipmanagement. The primary objective is to ensure that
employees are provided with adequate time off to maintain work-life balance, recover from
illness, and attend to personal family matters, while ensuring operational continuity across
our Mumbai and Chennai offices. This policy applies strictly to permanent shore staff employed by Kestrel Shipmanagement.

chunks.heading: Version: 3.3
chunks.text:
It
governs the accrual, usage, and administration of various leave types for office-based
personnel. Seafarers are covered by their own contracts and are not subject to this specific
document; they should contact the Crewing department for details regarding their respective
entitlements. All employees are expected to manage their leave responsibly in consultation with their line
managers to ensure that business operations are not adversely affected. This policy serves
as a guideline, and specific circumstances may require individual discussion with Human
Resources.

chunks.heading: Annual Leave
chunks.text:
Permanent shore staff are entitled to 26 days of annual leave per calendar year. This
entitlement is accrued at a rate of 2 days per month. Accrual begins from the first day of
employment, allowing employees to build up their balance progressively throughout the year. Employees may utilize their accrued annual leave for vacation, personal travel, or other
private matters. It is the responsibility of each employee to monitor their remaining
balance via the KestrelHR portal and to plan their time off accordingly.

chunks.heading: Annual Leave
chunks.text:

balance via the KestrelHR portal and to plan their time off accordingly.
While the company
encourages taking full annual leave entitlements to prevent burnout, employees must
coordinate with their line managers to ensure adequate coverage within the team.

chunks.heading: Carry Forward Rules
chunks.text:
There are specific restrictions regarding the carry forward of unused annual leave.
Employees may carry forward a maximum of 10 days into the next year. This cap is strictly

chunks.heading: Carry Forward Rules
chunks.text:
enforced to encourage regular time off and prevent excessive accumulation of leave
liabilities.
Carried-forward days must be used by 31 March or they lapse. Any balance exceeding the
10-day limit that is not utilized by this deadline will be forfeited. Employees are advised
to review their carry-forward status in early February to plan the use of these days before
the end of the financial year.

chunks.heading: Sick Leave
chunks.text:
Employees are entitled to 12 days of paid sick leave per year. This leave is intended for
periods of illness or injury that prevent the employee from performing their duties. It is
designed to support employees during unexpected health issues without immediate financial
penalty.
To claim sick leave, employees must notify their line manager as soon as possible on the
first day of absence. If the absence extends beyond a single day, continued notification is
required until the employee returns to work.

chunks.heading: Medical Certification
chunks.text:
A medical certificate is required for more than 2 consecutive days of sick leave. This
documentation serves to verify the authenticity of the illness and ensure that leave records
are accurate. Employees must submit the medical certificate to the HR department or upload
it via the KestrelHR portal within five working days of returning to work. Failure to
provide the required certification may result in the absence being treated as unpaid leave
or deducted from annual leave entitlements, at the discretion of management.

chunks.heading: Parental Leave
chunks.text:
Kestrel Shipmanagement supports employees during significant family events through dedicated
parental leave provisions. These policies are designed to support work-life integration and
family bonding.

chunks.heading: Maternity Leave
chunks.text:
Female employees who give birth are entitled to 26 weeks of paid maternity leave. This leave
is intended to provide sufficient time for recovery and early childcare. Employees wishing
to avail themselves of this benefit must inform their line manager and HRBP at least eight
weeks prior to the expected due date, if possible, to allow for adequate planning and
handover arrangements.

chunks.heading: Paternity Leave
chunks.text: Male employees who become fathers are entitled to 10 working days of paid paternity leave.

chunks.heading: Paternity Leave
chunks.text:
This leave is available to support the employee during the immediate post-birth period. The
leave must be taken within 3 months of the child's birth. Employees should coordinate with
their line manager to schedule this leave, ensuring that critical tasks are managed during
their absence.

chunks.heading: Bereavement Leave
chunks.text:
In the event of a family loss, employees are granted compassionate time off. Kestrel
Shipmanagement provides 5 days of paid bereavement leave for the death of an immediate
family member. Immediate family members are defined as spouse, child, parent, or sibling.
This leave is intended to allow employees time to attend funeral services and manage
immediate administrative and emotional matters following a loss. Employees should notify
their line manager as soon as possible after the event. HRBP support is available for any
additional assistance required during this period.

chunks.heading: Public Holidays and Compensatory Off
chunks.text:
The company observes 12 public holidays per year. These holidays are recognized across both
Mumbai and Chennai offices, subject to local statutory requirements. The list for the coming
year is published in December, allowing employees to plan their schedules accordingly.
Employees are not required to work on these days unless specifically arranged due to
critical business needs, in which case standard compensation procedures apply.

chunks.heading: Working on Public Holidays
chunks.text:
If an employee is required to work on a public holiday due to operational necessities, they
earn one compensatory day off. This entitlement ensures that employees who sacrifice their
holiday time are fairly compensated with equivalent rest time. The compensatory day off must be taken within 30 days of working the public holiday. Employees should coordinate with their line manager to schedule this day off at a mutually
convenient time.

chunks.heading: Working on Public Holidays
chunks.text:
should coordinate with their line manager to schedule this day off at a mutually
convenient time.
Failure to take the compensatory day off within the 30-day window may
result in the forfeiture of that specific day, unless extenuating circumstances are approved
by HR.

chunks.heading: Applying for Leave
chunks.text:
All leave requests must be submitted through the KestrelHR portal. This centralized system
ensures accurate recording of leave balances and facilitates approval workflows. Employees
are responsible for ensuring that their leave applications are complete and accurate before
submission.
Advance Notice Requirements

chunks.heading: Applying for Leave
chunks.text:
For standard annual leave or other planned absences, employees must adhere to specific
advance notice periods. Leave longer than 3 days must be applied for at least 14 days in
advance. This requirement allows line managers sufficient time to arrange coverage and
manage workflow disruptions. Shorter leaves may be approved with less notice, subject to
operational requirements and manager discretion.

chunks.heading: Applying for Leave
chunks.text:
may be approved with less notice, subject to
operational requirements and manager discretion.
Emergency leave, such as sudden illness or bereavement, should be reported immediately via
phone or email to the line manager, followed by a formal entry in the KestrelHR portal upon
return or when able to do so.

chunks.heading: Leave During Probation
chunks.text:
New joiners accrue leave from day one of their employment. This means that the entitlement
begins building up immediately, regardless of probationary status. However, there are
restrictions on the utilization of this accrued time during the initial period of
employment. Employees may only take annual leave after completing 3 months of service. This restriction
applies to all permanent shore staff during their probationary period. Sick leave and other
statutory leaves remain available as per standard policy from day one.

chunks.heading: Leave During Probation
chunks.text:
period. Sick leave and other
statutory leaves remain available as per standard policy from day one.
Line managers should
be aware of this restriction when approving or denying leave requests for new joiners within
their first three months.

chunks.heading: Leave Encashment on Exit
chunks.text:
When an employee leaves the company, whether through resignation, retirement, or
termination, unused annual leave may be encashed. This provision ensures that employees are
compensated for time off they were unable to utilize due to the timing of their departure. Encashment is calculated based on the basic salary. The payout covers unused annual leave up
to a maximum of 30 days. Any balance exceeding this cap will not be paid out and will be
forfeited upon exit.

chunks.heading: Leave Encashment on Exit
chunks.text:
of 30 days. Any balance exceeding this cap will not be paid out and will be
forfeited upon exit.
Employees are encouraged to use their accrued leave before their last
working day to maximize their benefit, subject to approval from their line manager and HRBP.

chunks.heading: Contacts
chunks.text:
For any questions regarding this policy, clarification on entitlements, or assistance with
leave applications, employees should contact their HR business partner (HRBP). The HRBP is
the primary point of contact for all human resources matters and can provide personalized
guidance based on individual circumstances.
Contact details for the HRBPs covering the Mumbai and Chennai offices are available on the
internal company intranet and via the KestrelHR portal. For urgent matters outside of
business hours, employees should follow the emergency contact protocol outlined in the
employee handbook.
Kestrel Shipmanagement - Remote Work and Code of Conduct (HR-POL-07)

chunks.heading: Introduction and Purpose
chunks.text:
This policy outlines the operational guidelines for remote work arrangements and establishes
the ethical standards expected of all shore staff at Kestrel Shipmanagement. As our
organization continues to evolve, we recognize the importance of flexibility in how we work,
balanced against the need for accountability, security, and professional integrity. This
document serves as the definitive reference for hybrid working arrangements, equipment
usage, ethical conduct, and grievance procedures.

chunks.heading: Introduction and Purpose
chunks.text:
for hybrid working arrangements, equipment
usage, ethical conduct, and grievance procedures.
All employees are required to familiarize
themselves with these guidelines to ensure compliance with company standards and local labor
regulations.

chunks.heading: Hybrid and Remote Work
chunks.text:
Kestrel Shipmanagement supports a flexible work environment designed to enhance productivity
and work-life balance while maintaining strong team cohesion. The following rules govern
remote work eligibility and scheduling:

- Eligibility: Confirmed employees may work remotely up to 2 days per week, provided this
 arrangement is explicitly agreed upon with their manager. This agreement should be
 documented in the employee's file or shared calendar to ensure operational visibility.

chunks.heading: Hybrid and Remote Work
chunks.text:
should be
 documented in the employee's file or shared calendar to ensure operational visibility.
- Probationary Period: Employees currently on probation are required to work from the
 office exclusively. Remote work privileges are not available during this initial
 assessment phase to facilitate proper onboarding, mentorship, and cultural integration.

chunks.heading: Hybrid and Remote Work
chunks.text:
initial
 assessment phase to facilitate proper onboarding, mentorship, and cultural integration.
- Managerial Approval: Any request for remote work must be discussed and approved by the
 direct manager prior to implementation. Managers retain the right to deny remote work
 requests if business continuity or team collaboration requirements cannot be met.

chunks.heading: Working Hours and Availability
chunks.text:
To ensure seamless communication across teams and time zones, specific availability windows
are mandated for all shore staff, regardless of their physical location.

- Core Hours: The designated core hours are 10:00 to 16:00 IST. During this window, every
 employee must be reachable via standard company communication channels (email, instant
 messaging, and phone).

chunks.heading: Working Hours and Availability
chunks.text:
- Responsiveness: Employees are expected to respond to urgent inquiries within a
 reasonable timeframe during core hours. Failure to maintain availability during these
 specified times may be considered a breach of performance expectations.

- Flexibility Outside Core Hours: Work performed outside of core hours is permitted for
 confirmed employees with prior managerial approval, provided that total working hours do
 not exceed statutory limits and that rest periods are respected.

chunks.heading: Equipment and Allowances
chunks.text:
Kestrel Shipmanagement provides necessary tools to support remote work while ensuring data
security and operational efficiency. Financial allowances are also provided to offset the
costs associated with working from home.

- Internet Reimbursement: To support connectivity requirements, the company provides an
 internet reimbursement of INR 1,500 per month for remote work. This allowance is
 processed via payroll and requires employees to maintain valid proof of internet service
 payments if audited by the finance department.

chunks.heading: Equipment and Allowances
chunks.text:
to maintain valid proof of internet service
 payments if audited by the finance department.
- Company-L Provided Equipment: All necessary hardware, including laptops and peripherals,
 remains the property of Kestrel Shipmanagement. Employees are responsible for the
 safekeeping of these items while working remotely.

chunks.heading: Equipment and Allowances
chunks.text:
Employees are responsible for the
 safekeeping of these items while working remotely.
- Return of Assets: Company laptops must be returned within 7 days of the last working
 day. This applies to both voluntary resignations and terminations. Failure to return
 assets within this timeframe may result in deductions from final settlements or legal
 action to recover the equipment.

chunks.heading: Gifts and Hospitality
chunks.text:
To maintain objectivity and prevent undue influence, strict guidelines govern the acceptance
of gifts and hospitality from external parties.

- Vendor and Supplier Gifts: Employees may only accept gifts from vendors or suppliers if
 the value is no more than INR 2,000 per item. Any gift exceeding this threshold must be
 declined politely and reported to the compliance team.

chunks.heading: Gifts and Hospitality
chunks.text:
Any gift exceeding this threshold must be
 declined politely and reported to the compliance team.
- Recording Requirements: Every accepted gift, regardless of value, must be recorded in
 the official gift register. This log includes details such as the giver's name, date of
 receipt, description of the item, and estimated value. The register is subject to
 periodic audit by the internal audit department.

- Prohibited Items: Cash, cash equivalents, and gifts intended to influence business
 decisions are strictly prohibited under all circumstances.

chunks.heading: Conflicts of Interest
chunks.text:
Employees must act in the best interest of Kestrel Shipmanagement at all times. A conflict
of interest arises when an employee's personal interests interfere, or appear to interfere,
with their professional duties.

chunks.heading: Conflicts of Interest
chunks.text:
- Annual Declaration: A conflict of interest declaration must be submitted every year by
 30 April. This declaration requires employees to disclose any external business
 interests, family relationships with competitors, or other potential conflicts.

- Ongoing Disclosure: Employees must also report any new conflicts of interest immediately
 upon discovery, rather than waiting for the annual submission deadline.

chunks.heading: Conflicts of Interest
chunks.text:
of interest immediately
 upon discovery, rather than waiting for the annual submission deadline.
- Management Review: All submitted declarations are reviewed by the HR and Compliance
 departments. Where a conflict is identified, appropriate mitigation measures will be
 implemented, which may include recusal from specific decisions or reassignment of
 duties.

chunks.heading: Raising a Grievance
chunks.text:
Kestrel Shipmanagement is committed to resolving workplace issues fairly and efficiently.
The following procedure outlines the steps for raising and addressing grievances.

- Initial Step: Employees should raise their grievance first with the HR business partner
 assigned to their department. The HR business partner will conduct an initial review and
 attempt to facilitate a resolution.

chunks.heading: Raising a Grievance
chunks.text:
The HR business partner will conduct an initial review and
 attempt to facilitate a resolution.
- Escalation Path: If the issue remains unresolved after discussion with the HR business
 partner, the case may be escalated to the Grievance Committee. This committee comprises
 senior management representatives and is empowered to make binding decisions on
 workplace disputes.

- Resolution Timeline: The target is to resolve a grievance within 15 working days from
 the date of formal submission to the appropriate authority. Employees will be kept
 informed of the progress throughout the process.

chunks.heading: Prevention of Sexual Harassment
chunks.text:
Kestrel Shipmanagement maintains a zero-tolerance policy toward sexual harassment. We are
dedicated to providing a safe and respectful work environment for all staff members.

- Reporting Mechanism: Complaints regarding sexual harassment must be directed to the
 Internal Committee (IC). The IC is an independent body established specifically to
 handle such sensitive matters.

- Inquiry Process: Upon receipt of a complaint, the Internal Committee will initiate a
 formal inquiry. This process ensures confidentiality and impartiality while gathering
 all necessary facts.

chunks.heading: Prevention of Sexual Harassment
chunks.text:
This process ensures confidentiality and impartiality while gathering
 all necessary facts.
- Timeline for Resolution: The Internal Committee must complete its inquiry within 90 days
 from the date of filing the complaint. Both parties involved will be notified of the
 findings and any subsequent actions taken.

chunks.heading: Notice Period and Exit
chunks.text:
Clear procedures govern the termination of employment to ensure a smooth transition for both
the employee and the company.

chunks.heading: Notice Period and Exit
chunks.text:
- Confirmed Employees: The notice period for confirmed employees is 60 days. During this
 period, the employee is expected to continue fulfilling their duties, assist in
 knowledge transfer, and complete all exit formalities.

- Probationary Employees: For employees still on probation, the notice period is 15 days.
 This shorter duration reflects the preliminary nature of the employment relationship
 during the initial assessment phase.

chunks.heading: Notice Period and Exit
chunks.text:
the preliminary nature of the employment relationship
 during the initial assessment phase.
- Exit Formalities: All employees must complete an exit interview with HR and return all
 company property, including access cards, laptops, and documents, in accordance with the
 timelines specified in this policy. Failure to adhere to notice periods may impact final
 pay, experience letters, or future rehire eligibility.

*

*This policy is subject to periodic review by the Human Resources department. Any updates
will be communicated to all shore staff via official company channels.*
